newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to reveal housing fund securitization plan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to reveal housing fund securitization plan.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan will reveal on Tuesday the government's plans to securitize a multi-billion dollar deficit in a federal housing fund, officials said.

Finance Ministry officials said Malan and Sergio Cutolo, head of federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal, would give a news conference at 1130 local/1430 GMT to announce their plans for the so-called FCVS housing fund.
Malan has said the government had identified 12 billion reais in debt which would have to be securitized. Private sector estimates of the FCVS deficit run to 50 billion reais.

The government intends to use 30-year Treasury notes, with a 15-year grace period for principle and eight years grace for interest, to securitize the deficit, caused by populist housing policies since the FCVS fund was created in 1967.
The loss -- the difference between mortgage costs and what mortgage holders have been paying -- has yet to show up as debt in the government's accounts.
Officials acknowledge the securitization will increase net public sector debt but stress the measure will just be swapping old unrecognized debt for new.
The decree due to be revealed Tuesday is also expected to provide incentives for people holding federal mortgages to pay them off early, perhaps at a considerable discount.
Reports in July suggested the National Treasury expected to begin issuing between 15 billion reais and 20 billion reais in notes at the end of the year to start covering the deficit.
